w1.model_answer_md: Start every order's stopwatch at the time it was **due**, its place on the schedule, not when it was handed over. If there was no schedule (the old four runners), the handover is the start.

bridge.real: the stopwatch starts when the order was due

key_ideas.idea: the dispatcher never stops taking orders at their due time, even when every tray is out
an order with no free tray waits in line for one itself (the waiting happens per order, not at the door)
the next due time comes from the plan (the last due time plus the gap), not from 'now'
orders that went out late can be counted

accepted: queue the orders and keep the schedule running
a helper waits for trays so the dispatcher doesn't

w2.model_answer_md: Keep the schedule no matter what: take each order exactly when it's due. If no tray is free, **the order** waits in line for one, not the dispatcher. The next due time is the last due time plus the gap, never "now plus the gap", so nobody due during a stall is skipped.

bridge.real: take every order at its due time; an order with no tray waits for one

key_ideas.idea: round the position UP (9.9 becomes 10), so the clerk takes the tenth slip, the slow one

wrong_ideas.idea: average the slowest few slips, or interpolate between slips

w3.model_answer_md: Round the position **up**, not down: 9.9 becomes 10, so the clerk takes the tenth slip, the two-second one. Watch out for positions that are a hair over a whole number from rounding noise, like 999.0000000000001, which should count as 999.
